title: Android adds opt-in Gemini checks for message scams
friendlyTitle: Android will use Gemini to spot harder message scams
summary: Google is rolling out an opt-in enhanced protection mode in Google Messages that uses cloud Gemini models, inside Private AI Compute, to judge the intent of unknown senders, plus on-device Gemini Nano checks for unfamiliar links. Android will also warn about call-forwarding tricks and hide passwords and payment fields during screen sharing.
friendlySummary: Google is adding an optional Messages setting that uses Gemini to judge whether an unknown sender is running a scam, and to check unfamiliar links on the device. Android will also warn about secret call forwarding and hide passwords while you share your screen.
whyItMatters: Scam texts are a daily risk, and the new mode is meant to catch slower conversations that simple filters miss. It is opt-in, and Google says the cloud analysis is encrypted so the company cannot read it. A warning is still a reason to pause, not a guarantee.
friendlyWhyItMatters: These tools can catch scams that look like ordinary chats. Turn the setting on if you want it, and still pause before you tap a link or share a code.
